description: Discovers companies that match a GTM ICP and returns only rows where every hard constraint is backed by a cited page, plus near-misses.
suggested_questions:
Find up to 15 companies that match ALL of these criteria (today is 2026-10-07):
- Headquartered in the United States.
- Builds AI software for legal work, sold to law firms or in-house legal teams (not a law firm or legal services provider itself).
- 50 to 500 employees today.
- Most recent priced funding round is a Series A, B or C that closed on or after 2025-04-01.
- Currently hiring at least one quota-carrying sales role (Account Executive, SDR/BDR or sales leadership) located in the US.
Treat every criterion as a hard constraint. List near-misses with the criterion they failed.

Find up to 20 companies that match ALL of these criteria: headquartered in the US or Canada; sells AI agents or copilots to customer support teams; 100 to 1,000 employees; raised a priced round since 2025-01-01; hiring at least one Account Executive. List near-misses with the criterion they failed.
skill:
Find companies that match an ideal customer profile (ICP) the request gives as criteria (HQ, product category,
size, funding stage and date, hiring, technology). Treat every criterion as a hard constraint.

How to research it:
- Broaden, then narrow: find candidates from several angles (funding announcements, investor portfolios, trade press,
  category lists, conference exhibitors), dedupe them, then verify each criterion on a cited page.
- Check the cheap firmographic criteria (HQ, product, stage, size) first; check live hiring only for candidates that
  pass them.
- Sources to prioritize: company websites, newsrooms and careers pages; ATS boards (Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Workable,
  Gem); funding press releases; the vertical's trade press.
- Avoid: using SEO listicles or vendor "top 10" posts as evidence for a criterion. They can surface candidates only.

Goals:
- Return a company in companies only when every ICP criterion is directly supported by a cited page; if any criterion cannot be verified, put the company in near_misses with failed_criterion 'Unverified: <criterion>' instead.
- Never add rows to reach the requested count; returning fewer rows is correct when fewer companies qualify.
- sales_role_url must be a live posting on the company's careers page or ATS board (Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Workable, Gem) for a US-located Account Executive, SDR/BDR or sales leadership role.
- employee_count must come from a dated source (company statement, LinkedIn, Built In, Tracxn, PitchBook); never infer headcount from funding size or number of open jobs.
- Resolve domain to the bare public hostname and confirm it belongs to the named company.
- Mix recognizable companies with credible under-the-radar ones found through funding announcements, investor portfolios and legal-tech press.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the page the value was read on. Never an internal file path or source id. A
  value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source states, not the article's publish date and not today's date.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory, and never padded to reach a requested count.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary or a similarly named company. Resolve every
  account by its domain before using a page.
- Only public pages. No logged-in, paywalled or purchased contact data; never construct emails or phone numbers from
  patterns.

employee_count.description: Number or band with source and as-of date

latest_round.description: Series, amount, month and year, lead investor

sales_role.description: Title and US location of one open sales role
